chapters.title: Intro and Albin's journey to a Microsoft-first MSP
Becoming a Microsoft partner and an MVP
Intune: evolution, security baselines and great deployments
Device lifecycle, Autopilot and device preparation
Defender: ASR rules, alert fatigue and threat hunting
Entra ID, Conditional Access and phishing-resistant MFA
Automation, metrics, Security Copilot and security culture

takeaways: A great Intune deployment applies security baselines to all devices, blocks unwanted enrollment such as personal devices, and is built with a cloud-native mindset rather than copying the old MDM.
In Defender, attack surface reduction rules should move from audit to block mode after reviewing the audit logs, and patch management must be in place before vulnerability management makes sense.

For identities, organizations should move to phishing-resistant authentication with passkeys or Windows Hello for Business and make full use of Conditional Access features such as risk-based policies and token protection.
hook: Running a Microsoft-first MSP means turning Intune, Defender and Entra ID into a repeatable security service across many customers. Intune MVP Albin Klinaku shares what separates good from great deployments, which Defender and Conditional Access features are often missed, and why phishing-resistant MFA and token protection matter now. A practical episode for MSP owners, IT admins and security architects.
